science.title: Unpacking societal barriers to technology adoption: a multi-theoretical analysis of user behavior in last mile delivery applications in urban developing contexts
science.description: Last-mile delivery (LMD) applications are expanding rapidly in developing urban contexts; however, technology adoption and continued use remain uneven due to societal and geographic barriers. This study investigates how digital literacy-related capabilities and constraints impact LMD app adoption outcomes in Alexandria, with a focus on user behavior as a mediator and district-level differences as a contextual moderator. A cross-sectional survey was conducted across Alexandria’s East, Middle, and West districts (N = 2120). The measurement and structural models were evaluated using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) in AMOS, which included confirmatory factor analysis, model fit assessment, and multi-group comparisons across districts. The results indicate that digital literacy-related constructs significantly shape user behavior toward LMD apps, which in turn influences subjective well-being and social inclusion. Indirect effects reveal both beneficial and potentially adverse pathways, highlighting the paradoxical role of digital literacy. District-level comparisons indicate meaningful geographic variation in key relationships. By integrating UTAUT and SST, this study explains LMD adoption as both a technological and socially embedded process. The findings offer implications for platform design and public policy aimed at reducing intra-city adoption inequalities and strengthening inclusive digital participation.

science.title: Spatio-temporal clustering characteristics of hepatitis B in China: an 18-year study
science.description: To describe the spatiotemporal characteristics of hepatitis B in China and to identify its possible hotspots and potential high-risk areas. A retrospective, province-level ecological analysis of hepatitis B surveillance data. Global Moran’s I and local Moran’s I were calculated using GeoDa 1.16 to explore the spatial clustering characteristics from 2004 to 2021, and the results of the spatiotemporal scan analysis were obtained using SaTScan 10.1 to identify cluster areas from 2004 to 2018. From 2004 to 2021, the number of hepatitis B incident cases in China increased from 916,426 in 2004 to 976,233 in 2021 (AAPC = 0.38%, P = 0.613), which is not statistically significant. From 2018 to 2021, High-High cluster areas of hepatitis B incidence rates in China were concentrated in the southeast; from 2004 to 2019, High-Low cluster areas of hepatitis B mortality rates were concentrated in Beijing and Shanghai. During the 18-year study period, the crude mortality rate showed a statistically significant decline with an average annual decline of 4.03%. Hepatitis B high-risk areas were concentrated in northwestern and southeastern coastal regions of China, while death counts were clustered in the northwestern and eastern regions.

science.title: Collapsing stars could spawn mini-universes, offering new path to gravastars
science.description: Stars shine because atoms fuse in their interiors, releasing energy. When a very massive star has exhausted its nuclear fuel, radiation pressure can no longer provide sufficient counterforce to gravity. The star then collapses under its own mass until only a single point remains: the singularity.
